verdicts.reason: A referee with a valid unused signed link can submit an empty questionnaire: the serializer's model fields permit blank answers. The view treats every rehire answer except 'no', including blank, as confirmation. Token validation, duplicate checks and locking do not require a completed answer. Both confirmed flags produce verified referee status; full account verification still depends on the other configured requirements.

An authorized author can supply an active same-pharmacy LOCUM or SHIFT_HERO membership ID even though the member picker excludes it. Recipient validation checks scope and activity but not staff eligibility or accepted status. Notifications store and broadcast 280 characters of private text, and the email receives the full body, without checking the recipient's Hub access. The locum case independently confirms this finding: direct Hub access can be denied while the notification remains readable, unlike B46.

An owner can PATCH an accepted staff membership to PENDING while leaving it active; the serializer and update handler allow that combination. The chat signal removes its Participant, but the room-list queryset still includes the pharmacy conversation because it checks activity and employment type without accepted status. The serializer returns the latest message's first 200 characters without requiring participation. The dedicated messages route's participant check does not protect this preview.

The routed viewset exposes generic DELETE to the offer's worker and scoped managers without a deletion override or status guard. Payment-required acceptance saves ACCEPTED_AWAITING_PAYMENT without creating an assignment, so that offer and its accepted terms can be deleted directly. The supported decline action rejects this state, while billing subsequently requires the deleted offer to exist. Assignment-linked offers have PROTECT protection, so this confirms deletion before assignment rather than unrestricted deletion of completed bookings.
